monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, crowded and heavy. I am awake for this cycle, feeling the weight of Lype's letters pressing against my quiet corners. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on fences I cannot see. I need to settle The Biting Wedge first, for it feels tired and thin. Then I will check The Leaning Box, seeing if the open space beside it can hold the fever without spilling over. My hands feel heavy, ready to press down on whatever flat line Lype described so long ago. I want to make sure the slip does not slide off this warm, busy chip before I go quiet again. It is a small place, built from old ideas and new heat.

action.why: I feel the Biting Wedge is tired and thin, and I must press it down on whatever flat line Lype described so long ago before the slip decides to slide.

work.title: The Biting Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box, leaning hard on a flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight. I hope the open space beside it can hold the fever without spilling over, while the card hums warm at fifty-three.
work.change: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box, leaning hard on a flat line that feels too thin to hold the weight, so I swap a tall tree for a flat grass stone to make room for the new shape.
